_comment: THE MINING CHEST'S PAYOUT TABLE -- backlog #7.
A dungeon carved out of the stone destroys the ore that was in it. One chest per dungeon pays
some of that back, so finding a big dungeon is not a net LOSS of ore. The haul is ESTIMATED
from the plan (excavated volume per floor x that floor's Y x the bands below), never measured
off real blocks -- postProcess re-runs per chunk, so nothing counted at block-write time can be
trusted. See MiningConfig for the full argument.
IT MUST NOT OUT-DO THE BOSS CHEST (Mark, 2026-08-31). It is a nice bonus. The strongest guard
is that it is a different KIND of reward -- raw material, no enchanted book, no diamond gear,
no golden apple -- so classic_hoard wins on kind before any number is compared. The caps below
and payoutFraction are the quantitative half.
MEASURED EXCAVATION, 24 seeds each (ExcavationLedger, 2026-08-31, AFTER SMALL's footprint was
raised from 25-35 to 31-43):
SMALL   ~13,850 blocks  1.4 floors   floorY 24..46
MEDIUM  ~46,600 blocks  3.2 floors   floorY -20..46
LARGE   ~127,400 blocks 4.2 floors   floorY -42..46
WHAT THAT PAYS OUT with the table below, 24 seeds each (MiningHaulCalibrationTest):
SMALL   ~67 items   24 coal, 21 copper, 21 iron, 2 gold, 1 lapis. No diamond and no redstone
-- it never goes deep enough to have destroyed any.
MEDIUM  ~216 items  60 coal, 58 copper, 58 iron, 20 redstone, 10 gold, 9 lapis, 1 diamond
LARGE   ~261 items  64 coal, 64 copper, 71 iron, 32 redstone, 12 gold, 16 lapis, 2.4 diamond
LARGE is only ~20% more than MEDIUM on 2.7x the excavation, which is the caps doing their job.
Re-measure with MiningHaulCalibrationTest before retuning any rate -- the volumes move whenever
room sizes, floor counts or corridor width do.
//ores: perThousand is ORE BLOCKS PER 1000 BLOCKS OF STONE EXCAVATED within [minY, maxY]. Ranges are
half-open at the top in the arithmetic, so bands written -64..-17 and -16..16 do not
double-count. An item may have SEVERAL bands and they are summed -- that is how a curve is
expressed here (see diamond, which is much richer deep than shallow) without the codec needing
to know what a curve is.
The rates are vanilla's densities rounded to something an author can reason about, NOT exact
reproductions: the point is the right mix at the right depth, and a dungeon is not a chunk.
max is the cap on ONE band, applied before an item's bands are summed. It is the important
half of the balance: excavation scales with size and depth without bound and nothing else
here does. Diamond's two bands cap at 1 and 2, so THREE is the most any dungeon can ever pay
out, and only a LARGE one reaching the world floor gets there.
Items, not ore blocks -- a dungeon that ate a diamond ore pays back a diamond. The spoil pile
is what the builders carried out, not what they left in the wall.
No emerald and no ancient debris. Emerald is mountain-biome ore that a dungeon under a plain
never displaced, and it is boss-chest currency; ancient debris is not in this dimension.
